newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana sends troops to Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: Ghana sends troops to Sierra Leone.

text.p: Ghana sent troops to Sierra Leone on Sunday to help evacuate its nationals and to join a Nigerian-led regional force, a government statement said.

It gave no troop numbers but said: "The command of the contingent will also be involved in the negotiations for a political settlement of the crisis in Sierra Leone, following which the Ghanaian contingent may be deployed to help stabilise the situation".

The government recalled Deputy Foreign Minister Victor Gbeho from the Organisation of African Unity summit in Harare to join a negotiating team of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS).
Nigeria currently holds the ECOWAS presidency and has been trying to persuade the coup leaders to stand down, both through negotiations and the threat of a military strike.
Ghana's President Jerry Rawlings opted to stay away from the Harare summit to monitor the situation in Sierra Leone.
Gbeho has been active in the past in peace negotiations with the warring factions in Liberia, where the West African ECOMOG force was first deployed in 1990.
The Nigerian-led force's numbers in Sierra Leone were boosted on Saturday by the arrival of three battalions of Guinean troops.
ECOMOG now numbers about 3,000 men in Sierra Leone, backed by Nigerian ships as well as helicopters based in Liberia.

Military sources said on Saturday the Ghanaians' task would be to replace the Nigerians securing the international airport at Lungi, across the river estuary to the north of the capital, and the smaller airport at Hastings, east of Freetown near the Nigerian base.
The Ghanaian deployment is codenamed Operation Ogyefo, the word for saviour in the Akan language.
